turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, before anyone called me. Who decided that?
You need an answer today. I've been waiting a week for one, Hale, so you go first: who entered that zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Either Owen admits it in writing by Friday at 3 PM or the zero goes on his transcript.

Admits what, Hale? You've shown me nothing, and under your own procedure a first concern gets a supervised reassessment, not a confession by Friday at 3 PM. I'm writing down that you said "admits it in writing," and when we're done I'm walking that sentence straight to the principal's office.
Those are the only two options. Pick one.

Neither. My son wrote that essay, and he won't sign a lie because you've decided he's guilty without showing anyone a single document. Either you put your evidence on this desk right now, or I'm going upstairs.
